subject: Archaeology
title: Plaster Casts: Frozen in Time
description: A micro-lesson that makes Plaster Casts: Frozen in Time usable.

hook.text: In 1863, an archaeologist poured plaster into holes in the ash and created haunting casts of Pompeii's dead.

buildup.text: Giuseppe Fiorelli realized that bodies had decomposed, leaving hollow voids in the hardened volcanic debris.

discovery.text: The casts captured people in their final moments — a mother shielding a child, a dog straining at its chain.

twist.text: CT scans of the casts reveal bones, teeth, and expressions. One man appears to be screaming.

climax.text: Over 100 casts have been made. They turned an archaeological site into a memorial, making ancient death personal.

punchline.text: Volcanic ash erased their faces. Plaster gave them back.

quiz.question: How were the famous plaster casts of Pompeii created?
options: Artists sculpted them based on skeletal remains found at the site
Plaster was poured into body-shaped voids left in hardened ash
3D scanning reconstructed the victims from bone fragments
